issues.problem: 中文“有意含糊”、英文“deliberately ambiguous”把含糊说成是有意为之。麦迪逊只写了这个格式含糊，以及起草目的是争取异议者，没有说含糊本身是刻意设计的。

evidence.quote: This ambiguous form had been drawn up by Mr. Gouverneur Morris, in order to gain the dissenting members

issues.rationale: 麦迪逊只说这个格式含糊，并说起草目的是争取异议者，没有说含糊是刻意设计的。dek 中文“有意含糊”改为“含糊”，英文“deliberately ambiguous”改为“ambiguous”。

issues.problem: 此句位于富兰克林讲话之前，说会上已有几位成员“公开表示过异议”。证据包里当天的公开异议（伦道夫、格里等）都出现在讲话之后。F-E18 还记载富兰克林写讲稿时并不知道会有成员拒签。讲话时只能说仍可能有人持异议。

On the last day of the Constitutional Convention: a deliberately ambiguous signing formula, several readings of what a signature meant, three refusals, and a sun painted on the back of the presiding officer's chair.

edits.before: September 17, 1787, the last day of the Constitutional Convention. The engrossed Constitution had just been read aloud when Benjamin Franklin rose with a speech in his hand; Madison's notes say he had written it out for his own convenience, and Mr. Wilson read it to the hall. The meeting was about to dissolve. Several members openly voiced objections to the document on the table. One question before them: sign it or not, and how.
edits.after: September 17, 1787, the last day of the Constitutional Convention. The engrossed Constitution had just been read aloud when Benjamin Franklin rose with a speech in his hand; Madison's notes say he had written it out for his own convenience, and Mr. Wilson read it to the hall. The meeting was about to dissolve. Some members might still have objections to the document on the table. One question before them: sign it or not, and how.

edits.before: 他随即动议成员签字，并提出一个现成的格式：“经出席各州一致同意，于会议中完成，9月17日……为此，我们在此签名作证。”麦迪逊记下一笔内情：这个有意含糊的格式由古弗尼尔·莫里斯起草，为的是争取异议者，交到富兰克林手上提出，好让它有更大的成功机会。
edits.after: 他随即动议成员签字，并提出一个现成的格式：“经出席各州一致同意，于会议中完成，9月17日……为此，我们在此签名作证。”麦迪逊记下一笔内情：这个含糊的格式由古弗尼尔·莫里斯起草，为的是争取异议者，交到富兰克林手上提出，好让它有更大的成功机会。

edits.before: 这一天的争议几乎都绕着同一个动作：在文件末尾写上名字。一种解释是，莫里斯起草的那个格式把“签字”拆成了两个问题——你证明什么，你承诺什么。莫里斯和布朗特只认“出席各州一致”这个事实；英格索尔读作推荐；平克尼要求签名就该是承诺；伦道夫则认为两者拆不开，签了就是签了，格式再软也一样。作者推断，正因为它对不同的人意味着不同的事，多数人才能站到同一行名字底下；代价是，这行名字的含义从此需要解释。
edits.after: 这一天的争议几乎都绕着同一个动作：在文件末尾写上名字。一种解释是，莫里斯起草的那个格式把“签字”拆成了两个问题——你证明什么，你承诺什么。莫里斯把这个格式解读为只关乎“出席各州一致”这一事实，布朗特据此表示可以只作证明、不作承诺；英格索尔读作推荐；平克尼要求签名就该是承诺；伦道夫则认为两者拆不开，签了就是签了，格式再软也一样。作者推断，正因为它对不同的人意味着不同的事，多数人才能站到同一行名字底下；代价是，这行名字的含义从此需要解释。

edits.before: Almost the whole day's argument circles a single act: writing a name at the foot of a page. On one reading, Morris's form split signing into two questions — what do you attest, and what do you commit to? Morris and Blount acknowledged only the fact that the states present were unanimous; Ingersoll read the signature as a recommendation; Pinckney held that it ought to be a commitment; Randolph thought the two inseparable, a signature however softly worded being still a signature. The author's inference: precisely because the act meant different things to different men could a majority stand beneath one row of names. The price was that the meaning of that row would need explaining ever after.
edits.after: Almost the whole day's argument circles a single act: writing a name at the foot of a page. On one reading, Morris's form split signing into two questions — what do you attest, and what do you commit to? Morris read the form as relating only to the fact that the states present were unanimous, and Blount, relieved by it, would attest that fact without committing himself; Ingersoll read the signature as a recommendation; Pinckney held that it ought to be a commitment; Randolph thought the two inseparable, a signature however softly worded being still a signature. The author's inference: precisely because the act meant different things to different men could a majority stand beneath one row of names; the price, on this inference, was that the meaning of that row would need explaining ever after.

edits.before: 会议官方日志及其他文件的去向也值得留意，它们和本篇所依据的麦迪逊笔记是两份不同的材料。同日的笔记里，金建议销毁会议日志或交主席保管，理由是日志若公开，会被想阻挠宪法的人利用；威尔逊倾向交主席保管（他一度更赞成销毁），说虚假说法可能流传，不应让反驳无从谈起；最终决定把日志及其他文件交主席保管，听候日后若依宪法成立的国会处置。至于富兰克林关于太阳的那段话，笔记记的是他望着椅背，对身边几位成员说的——那是对身边几个人说的话，不是对全场的正式演说。另外，本篇只写到1787年9月17日会议散会为止，不涉及宪法此后的批准与修正。

edits.before: The fate of the Convention's official Journals and other papers also deserves a look; they are a different set of papers from the Madison notes this piece relies on. In Madison's notes for the same day, King suggests that the Journals be destroyed or left in the president's custody, since made public they would be put to bad use by those wishing to prevent the Constitution's adoption; Wilson prefers the second course, though he had at one time liked the first best — false suggestions may be spread, and it should not be made impossible to contradict them — and the Journals and other papers are left with the president, subject to the order of Congress, if ever formed under the Constitution. As for Franklin and the sun, the notes record that he observed to a few members near him: an aside to those beside him, not a formal address to the whole hall. In any case, this piece stops at the adjournment of 17 September 1787 and touches neither ratification nor amendment.

issues.proposed: 中文改为“会要散了，会上仍可能有成员对这份文件持有异议。”英文改为“Some members might still have objections to the document on the table.”，并在本段 ev 中补上 F-E6。

issues.problem: 中文把“有意含糊”放在“麦迪逊记下一笔内情”之下，等于说这是麦迪逊的原话。原文只写“This ambiguous form”，英文版也只写 ambiguous，因此中英不对等。

evidence.quote: This ambiguous form had been drawn up by Mr. Gouverneur Morris

issues.proposed: 中文改为“这个含糊的格式由古弗尼尔·莫里斯起草，为的是争取异议者……”

issues.problem: “莫里斯和布朗特只认‘出席各州一致’这个事实”会让读者以为莫里斯本人只愿证明事实、不作承诺。证据中，莫里斯只是指出该格式仅关乎各州一致这一事实；他本人表示愿连同缺点接受方案，并服从多数决定。只有布朗特明确表示签名而不承诺自己。

evidence.quote: he should take it with all its faults
He remarked that the signing, in the form proposed, related only to the fact that the states present were unanimous.
would, without committing himself, attest the fact

issues.proposed: 中文改为“莫里斯把这个格式解读为只关乎‘出席各州一致’的事实，布朗特据此只作证明、不作承诺”。英文相应改为“Morris read the form as relating only to the fact that the states present were unanimous, and Blount signed on that basis without committing himself”。

issues.problem: 中文的“代价是……”仍在“作者推断”的句子之内。英文“The price was that the meaning of that row would need explaining ever after.”另起一句，脱离了 The author's inference 的标注，读起来像事实陈述，与中文不对等。
issues.proposed: 英文改为“The price, on this inference, was that…”，或并入前一句的推断之内。

issues.problem: 中文“官方日志”、英文“official Journals”，以及“它们和本篇所依据的麦迪逊笔记是两份不同的材料”这一判断，在证据包里都没有出处。证据只出现“Journals of the Convention”。

evidence.quote: the Journals of the Convention should be either destroyed, or deposited in the custody of the president

issues.proposed: 删去“官方/official”以及“两份不同的材料”一句，只写“会议日志（Journals）及其他文件的去向也值得留意”。

issues.problem: 中文再次写“那个有意含糊的格式”，英文写“the ambiguous form of 1787”，中英不一致。而且“有意”没有证据支持（见 F1）。

evidence.quote: This ambiguous form

issues.proposed: 中文改为“1787年那个含糊的格式”。
